full_judgment: 2. The petitioner, a co-operative society, filed the above Writ Petition No. 653 of 1995 stating, inter alia, that Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) Moulvibazar, the respondent No.1, on 12.7.88 gave lease of Chatla Beel Group Fishery to the petitioner society for the years of 1395-97 B.S. and then upon the execution of lease deed the petitioner on 14.4.1988 got delivery of possession of the above fishery after paying Tk.4,46,850/- as lease money for the entire lease period i.e. 1395-97 B.S.; besides, making the above payment the petitioner also made huge investment in the said fishery. But about seven months before the expiry of the term of the lease and also the fishing period, the respondents No.3, i.e. the Ministry of Land, cancelled the lease of the petitioner vide Memo No. Bhu-Ma-7, Maulvi-31/85/500/1(4) dated 2.10.1990 on the ground that decree has been passed in Title Suit No. 70 of 1988 in favour of M/S Sharping Fishermen Co-operative Society, hereinafter referred to as Sharping, who in the suit challenged the grant of lease in favour of the petitioner stating that Sharping earlier got lease of the above fishery but by cancelling the same illegally the fishery was lease to the petitioner for the period 1995-97. The respondent No.3 in view of the above decree, gave lease of the fishery to shaming for the period of 1397-1400 B.S. Though the petitioner submitted a representation addressed to the Upazilla Nirbahi Officer, Kulaura submitting that they suffered financial loss due to cancellation of their earlier lease just prior to the fishing period and considering the above representation the respondent No.3, by Memo No. Bhu-Ma/7 Moulvi-/91 dated 13.5.92, took the decision that after expiry of lease period of 1397-1400 already granted to the Sharping, the petitioner would be given lease for the years 1401-1403 B.S. upon adjustment of lease money amounting to Tk.4,46,850/-, which the petitioner earlier deposited and further, rent for the future lease was fixed @ 25% higher over the existing rent for the first year i.e. 1401 B.S. and 10% higher for the subsequent two years, i.e. 1402 and 1403 B.S.. Thereafter the petitioner in terms of the above memo repeatedly requested the respondents to execute the lease deed for the period 1401-1403 B.S. and gave delivery of possession of the said fishery in favour of the petitioner but the respondents did not execute the lease deed raising various pretexts. However, subsequently on the verbal direction of the respondent No.1, the petitioner went into the possession of the said fishery. Subsequently, the Respondent No.1 issued tae impugned order dated 1.3.95 stating that since the petitioner had enjoyed the said fishery from the year of 1395 to Bhadra 1397 B.S. the prior decision of the respondent No.2 vide memo dated 13.5.92 stands amended and directing the petitioner to deposit Tk. 2,82,875/- through DCR towards the payment of rent for the year of 1401 B.S. and also to get lease deed executed and take formal delivery of possession of the said fishery and thus the respondents changed their previous decision as per memo dated 13.5.1992 regarding adjustment of the amount of Tk. 4,46,850/- previously paid by the petitioner as lease money for the years 1395-97 B.S. The High Court Division on the basis of the above averment, issued Rule on 3.5.95 in Writ Petition No. 653 of 1995. Subsequently Deputy Commissioner, Moulvibazar, the respondent No.2, by letter dated 15.9.1996 which was addressed to the respondent No.3 asked the District Co-operative Officer, Sunamgonj District to take action against the petitioner and challenging the above letter dated 19.5.1996 that the petitioner moved the High Court Division and obtained rule on 27.10.1996 in Writ Petition No. 4380 of 1996. Then, after hearing, the High Court Division discharged both the Rules.
